TITLE: Investigating Non-Asymptotic Bounds for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Develop non-asymptotic sample-complexity guarantees for KernelSHAP, the most widely used randomized estimator for computing Shapley values, by analyzing its statistical properties and providing a theoretical framework for understanding its performance. Specifically, derive bounds on the variance and standard deviation of KernelSHAP's estimator, and provide a worst-case analysis of its convergence rate to the true Shapley values.
CONTROLS: Analyze the existing implementation of KernelSHAP in the SHAP library, compare the proposed bounds with the actual performance on real-world datasets, and conduct ablation studies on the impact of sampling distributions on the estimator's accuracy.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Developing non-asymptotic bounds for KernelSHAP should lead to a deeper understanding of its strengths and limitations, and shed light on its relative performance compared to other estimators. However, deriving tight bounds may require further research and may ultimately be challenging to obtain, especially for high-dimensional inputs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Empirical Comparison of Randomized Estimators for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Conduct an empirical evaluation of the performance of multiple randomized estimators for Shapley values, including KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and unbiased KernelSHAP, on a range of real-world datasets and models. Evaluate their accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency, and investigate the impact of dataset characteristics, such as dimensionality and sample size, on their performance.
CONTROLS: Benchmark the estimators against a set of ground-truth Shapley values, computed using exact methods for smaller datasets or approximated using multiple runs of KernelSHAP; compare their performance using metrics such as mean absolute error and standard deviation; and investigate the effect of hyperparameters, such as subsampling rates and kernel weights, on the estimators' accuracy.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: This comparison will help understand the strengths and weaknesses of each estimator, and provide practical guidance for choosing the best method for a given problem. However, directly computing ground-truth Shapley values may be challenging for large datasets, and approximating them using multiple runs of KernelSHAP may introduce bias.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leverage Score Analysis for Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of leverage scores, a concept from linear algebra, to improve the estimation of Shapley values for high-dimensional inputs. Specifically, analyze the relationship between the leverage scores of the subsets in the regression problem and the variance of the estimator, and explore the potential benefits of subset selection based on leverage scores.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of LeverageSHAP, which samples subsets based on their leverage scores, with other estimators, such as KernelSHAP and unbiased KernelSHAP, on a range of datasets and models; and investigate the impact of leverage score calculations on the computational efficiency of the estimators.
COST: 4100
PREDICTION: Leveraging leverage scores may provide a more efficient way to estimate Shapley values for high-dimensional inputs, but its effectiveness will depend on the specific characteristics of the datasets and models used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding the Impact of Subsampling on Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of subsampling rates on the accuracy and stability of randomized estimators for Shapley values, including KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and unbiased KernelSHAP. Analyze the trade-offs between subsampling rates, computational efficiency, and estimator accuracy, and provide guidelines for choosing optimal subsampling rates for different datasets and models.
CONTROLS: Conduct extensive experiments on a range of datasets and models to evaluate the impact of subsampling rates on estimator accuracy and stability; and compare the results with exact methods or other approximate methods for validation.
COST: 6800
PREDICTION: The optimal subsampling rate will depend on the specific characteristics of the datasets and models used, and may require careful tuning to achieve good estimator accuracy and stability. However, providing a systematic understanding of the trade-offs between subsampling rates and estimator performance will be valuable for practitioners.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Hybrid Leverage Score Analysis for Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Explore a hybrid approach that combines the ideas of leverage scores and subset selection with other established techniques, such as KernelSHAP or unbiased KernelSHAP. Specifically, investigate the use of leverage scores to select a subset of subsets for the regression problem, and then use a randomized estimator, such as KernelSHAP, to estimate the Shapley values for those selected subsets.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the hybrid approach with other estimators on a range of datasets and models; and investigate the impact of the hybrid approach on computational efficiency and estimator accuracy.
COST: 5100
PREDICTION: The hybrid approach may provide a more efficient way to estimate Shapley values for high-dimensional inputs, but its effectiveness will depend on the specific characteristics of the datasets and models used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Computation of Shapley Values for Large Models using Approximate Methods
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of approximate methods, such as randomized estimators or sparse regression, to efficiently compute Shapley values for large models with high-dimensional input spaces. Analyze the trade-offs between accuracy and computational efficiency, and provide guidelines for choosing the most suitable approximate method for different datasets and models.
CONTROLS: Implement and compare the performance of various approximate methods on a range of large models and datasets; and validate the results against exact methods or other approximate methods.
COST: 9600
PREDICTION: Approximate methods can significantly reduce the computational cost of computing Shapley values for large models, but may compromise accuracy. Careful tuning of the approximation parameters will be necessary to achieve a good trade-off between accuracy and efficiency.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Unbiased Empirical Comparison of Randomized Estimators for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Revise the empirical comparison of randomized estimators to account for potential biases in the evaluation metrics, such as mean absolute error (MAE). Specifically, investigate the use of debiasing techniques, such as de-biased MAE or subsampling-based de-biasing, to ensure that the comparison is unbiased and accurate.
CONTROLS: Implement the debiasing techniques and re-run the empirical comparison using the debiased metrics; and evaluate the impact of debiasing on the relative performance of the estimators.
COST: 8100
PREDICTION: Debiasing the evaluation metrics is crucial to ensure that the comparison of randomized estimators is fair and reliable. However, the effectiveness of debiasing techniques may depend on the specific characteristics of the datasets and models used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analysis of Uncertainty in Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the propagation of uncertainty in Shapley value estimation, particularly when using randomized estimators. Analyze the sources of uncertainty, such as noise in the data or model variability, and propose methods to quantify and visualize the uncertainty associated with the estimated Shapley values.
CONTROLS: Use techniques such as Bayesian inference or bootstrap resampling to quantify the uncertainty in the estimated Shapley values; and visualize the results using methods such as credible intervals or contour plots.
COST: 14400
PREDICTION: Understanding the uncertainty in Shapley value estimation is crucial to provide confidence intervals or other uncertainty measures for the estimated values. However, the complexity of the problem may make it challenging to fully capture the sources of uncertainty and provide accurate uncertainty quantification.

TITLE: Scalable Implementation of Shapley Value Estimation for High-Performance Computing
PROPOSAL: Develop a scalable and parallelizable implementation of Shapley value estimation using high-performance computing (HPC) frameworks such as OpenMP, CUDA, or MPI. Investigate the performance benefits of parallelization and identify potential bottlenecks in the implementation.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the parallelized implementation with existing serial implementations; and evaluate the scalability of the parallelized implementation on large-scale datasets.
COST: 18695.6268655256
PREDICTION: A scalable implementation of Shapley value estimation can significantly reduce the computation time for large-scale datasets, but may require careful optimization of the parallelization strategy to achieve good performance.

TITLE: Case Study: Applying Shapley Value Estimation to Real-World Predictive Modeling
PROPOSAL: Conduct a comprehensive case study on the application of Shapley value estimation to a real-world predictive modeling problem, such as credit risk assessment, medical diagnosis, or personalized recommendation. Evaluate the effectiveness of Shapley value estimation in providing interpretable insights into the predictive model's behavior and decision-making process.
CONTROLS: Collaborate with domain experts to identify a relevant real-world use case; collect and preprocess the data; implement Shapley value estimation using one of the proposed methods; and conduct thorough evaluation and analysis of the results.
COST: 24000
PREDICTION: A case study on the application of Shapley value estimation to a real-world predictive modeling problem can provide valuable insights into the practical benefits and limitations of the approach, but may require substantial effort to identify and prepare a suitable use case, collect and preprocess the data, and ensure that the results are accurate and interpretable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing a Long-term Temporal Context Model for Satellite Image Time Series Analysis
PROPOSAL: We will implement a Temporal Transformers (T-Tran) model as a baseline to capture long-range dependencies between satellite images. Specifically, we will utilize the Transformer encoder from BERT and fine-tune it on a dataset of globally distributed satellite images, focusing on Earth observation tasks such as land-cover classification and change detection.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to a traditional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model that processes a fixed-length window of consecutive images, and a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) model that utilizes a relatively short-term recurrent context.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: We expect T-Tran to outperform CNN and RNN models in change description and forecasting tasks by capturing more nuanced temporal relationships, but performance might degrade for extremely long sequences due to vanishing gradients.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhancing Temporal Understanding with Multi-Modal Fusion
PROPOSAL: We will extend the T-Tran model from proposal 1 by incorporating multi-modal fusion: we will include a sequence of sensor metadata (e.g., spectral bands, acquisition dates) as an additional input modality, and condition the T-Tran model on dense and spatially aware features extracted from a U-Net (UNet) architecture applied to the satellite images. This will allow the model to leverage both the visual and ancillary information present in the dataset.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the multi-modal T-Tran model to the baseline T-Tran model from proposal 1, and also experiment with fusing the sensor metadata and UNet features at different levels (e.g., before and after self-attention).
COST: 2800
PREDICTION: We anticipate that incorporating multi-modal information will lead to improved performance on tasks that leverage both visual and ancillary data, such as land-cover classification and change detection, but might compromise performance on purely visual tasks.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Enhancing Temporal Understanding with Multi-Modal Fusion
PROPOSAL: We will modify proposal 2 by incorporating a novel attention mechanism, Conditional Hyperbolic Tangent Attention (CHTA), that learns to weigh the importance of different sensor metadata features based on the visual content of the images. This will allow the model to selectively focus on the most relevant metadata features when generating the satellite image sequence.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the CHTA-based multi-modal T-Tran model to the original multi-modal T-Tran model from proposal 2, and also experiment with using other attention mechanisms (e.g., self-attention, dot-product attention).
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: We expect CHTA to improve performance on tasks that leverage both visual and ancillary data by selectively focusing on the most relevant metadata features, but might require careful hyperparameter tuning to prevent over_specialization on certain types of metadata.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dual-Task Learning for Simultaneous Change Description and Future Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will train a single T-Tran model to perform both change description and future forecasting tasks simultaneously, using a dual-task learning approach. The model will be trained with a shared encoder and task-specific decoders: a language generator for change description and a pixel-wise predictor for future forecasting. We will concatenate the embedding spaces of the language generator and pixel-wise predictor to facilitate knowledge sharing between the two tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the dual-task T-Tran model to separate T-Tran models trained for each task individually, and also experiment with different dual-task learning approaches (e.g., task-agnostic vs task-specific decoders).
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the dual-task learning approach will improve performance on both change description and future forecasting tasks by sharing knowledge between the two tasks, but might require careful tuning of the task-specific decoders to avoid overfitting to the primary task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Future Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will develop a Temporal Consistency Metric (TCM) to evaluate the temporal consistency of future forecasts. TCM will assess the similarity between the historical and forecasted image sequences using a combination of spatial and temporal metrics (e.g., SSIM, PSNR, optical flow). We will also incorporate a user study to ensure that the TCM captures human intuition of temporal consistency.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of TCM to existing metrics (e.g., mean absolute error, peak signal-to-noise ratio) and experiment with different weighting schemes for the spatial and temporal components of the metric.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: We expect TCM to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of temporal consistency, but might require careful tuning of the metric to balance the contributions of spatial and temporal components, and to account for various types of temporal inconsistencies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Incorporating Causal Inference for Understanding Change Dynamics
PROPOSAL: We will develop a causal inference approach to understand the underlying dynamics of change in satellite image time series. We will use a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to learn a probabilistic representation of the change process, and then utilize causal discovery algorithms (e.g., PC algorithm, GES) to identify the causal relationships between the variables governing the change.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the causal inference approach to traditional approaches that do not incorporate causal inference, and experiment with different causal discovery algorithms and VAE architectures.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: We anticipate that incorporating causal inference will provide valuable insights into the underlying dynamics of change, but might require careful tuning of the VAE and causal discovery algorithms to account for the complex temporal relationships between variables.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Incorporating Causal Inference for Understanding Change Dynamics
PROPOSAL: We will modify proposal 5 to incorporate a temporal causal graph into the VAE architecture, allowing the model to learn causal relationships that vary over time. We will use a temporal causal factorization to decompose the causal relationships into temporal and causal components, and then utilize a temporal causal inference algorithm (e.g., Temporal Causal PC algorithm) to learn the parameters of the model.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the temporal causal VAE to the original causal inference approach from proposal 5, and experiment with different temporal causal factorization techniques and causal inference algorithms.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: We expect the temporal causal VAE to provide even more accurate insights into the underlying dynamics of change, but might require careful tuning of the temporal causal factorization and causal inference algorithms to avoid overfitting to the temporal component.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fault-Tolerant Forecasts through Model-Based Uncertainty Estimation
PROPOSAL: We will develop a model that not only forecasts the future satellite images but also estimates the uncertainty associated with each forecast. We will use a Bayesian neural network to learn the posterior distribution over the model parameters, and then use this distribution to estimate the uncertainty of the forecasts. We will also use this uncertainty information to generate fault-tolerant forecasts that are robust to potential errors.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the fault-tolerant forecasts to traditional forecasts without uncertainty estimation, and experiment with different Bayesian neural network architectures and uncertainty estimation techniques.
COST: 6400
PREDICTION: We expect the fault-tolerant forecasts to significantly improve the robustness of the forecasts, but might require careful tuning of the Bayesian neural network and uncertainty estimation techniques to avoid overestimating or underestimating the uncertainty.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Validation on Large-Scale Satellite Imagery Datasets
PROPOSAL: We will validate our approach on large-scale real-world satellite imagery datasets such as Planet Labs' Sat-io dataset and the NASA Landsat 8 dataset. We will download and pre-process the data, and then evaluate our approach on a variety of tasks including change description, future forecasting, and fault-tolerant forecasting. We will also compare our results to state-of-the-art baselines and partner with satellite imaging companies to explore potential applications of our approach.
CONTROLS: We will experiment with different dataset partitions, task combinations, and evaluation metrics to ensure the robustness of our approach.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: We expect our approach to perform well on large-scale real-world datasets, but might require careful tuning of the approach to account for differences in dataset format, quality, and annotation, as well as potential challenges related to data privacy and scalability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Towards a Unified Framework for Satellite Image Time Series Analysis
PROPOSAL: We will attempts to unify the various approaches developed in this paper into a single, comprehensive framework for satellite image time series analysis. This framework will integrate long-term temporal context modeling, multi-modal fusion, dual-task learning, fault-tolerant forecasting, and real-world validation into a cohesive architecture. We will also provide a modular implementation of the framework, allowing researchers to easily add or modify components.
CONTROLS: We will experiment with different architectural configurations and component combinations to validate the unified framework.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: We expect the unified framework to provide a significant advance in the field of satellite image time series analysis, enabling researchers to tackle a wide range of tasks and applications with a single, scalable, and modular architecture. However, the complexity of the framework may require significant computational resources and expertise to develop and deploy.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Updating Final-Layer Weights vs. Model Freezing with Adapters in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of online gradient descent with final-layer weight updates versus model freezing with adapters for pre-trained state-of-the-art forecasting models (LSTM, GRU, Transformer) across six real-world datasets (OpenWeatherMap, TrafficFlow, EnergyGeneration, USAExchangeRate, SolarEnergy, ElectricityPrices). For each dataset, experiment with three random initialization strategies for adapters, three loss functions (MSE, MAE, Huber), and one baseline where no adapter is used. The performance metric will be a weighted average of mean absolute error (MAE) and symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE).
CONTROLS: The baseline of frozen model without adapter, a variant with OGD where the gradients are estimated from a small batch of recent samples instead of a single observation.
COST: 2341.37 
PREDICTION: Expected results will show comparable performance between models with updated final-layer weights and those with frozen models and adapter updates; higher loss functions will have smaller performance gaps. This method might fail to differentiate between the two update strategies due to the small number of adapter initializations and datasets.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of Adaptation Components in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of different adaptation components on performance, considering six components: output adapter, input adapter, linear adapter, ensemble weight adapter, fully connected adapter, and high-rank scaling coefficient adapter. Evaluate their performance in both model freezing and online gradient descent settings using the same six real-world datasets and pre-trained forecasting models (LSTM, GRU, Transformer) as in proposal 1. Compare their performance against a baseline where no adapter is used, as well as against the final-layer weight update baseline from proposal 1. Utilize a two-stage ablation study to remove components one by one, analyzing the loss in performance at each step.
CONTROLS: Baselines from proposal 1, a variant with OGD where gradients are estimated from a small batch of recent samples, and a random initialization baseline where adapters' parameters are randomly initialized.
COST: 3600 
PREDICTION: Expected results will show that a combination of output and input adapters performs best, providing a better trade-off between accuracy and stability. Alas, high-rank scaling coefficient adapters might underperform, showing the theory behind them has yet to be justified by empirical evidence.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Understanding the Impact of Delayed Feedback in Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of delayed feedback on performance in multi-step forecasting by introducing a lag in gradient computation. In a pre-trained Transformer-based forecasting model, gradually increase the forecasting horizon H while introducing a lag by delaying the computation of the true values for a forecasted step by H, (H+1), or more steps. Evaluate performance on a selection of three real-world datasets (TrafficFlow, USAExchangeRate, SolarEnergy) using a weighted average of mean absolute error (MAE) and symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE). Additionally, vary the model's architecture by modifying the number of layers and attention heads to study their impact on resilience to delayed feedback.
CONTROLS: A baseline without lag, a variant with OGD where gradients are estimated from a small batch of recent samples, and a model with increased capacity (more layers or attention heads) but no lag.
COST: 3780 
PREDICTION: Expected results will show that introducing a lag in feedback significantly degrades performance, especially in higher horizons; models with a higher capacity may be less impacted, but at the cost of increased training time.

ACTION: REVISE 3 
TITLE: Understanding the Impact of Delayed Feedback in Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Expand the previous proposal to include a comparison of different update strategies under delayed feedback. Instead of just introducing a lag, experiment with different update frequencies (e.g., update every other step, update only when a certain amount of information is available) and strategies (e.g., update with average past gradients, update with the last available gradient) for the pre-trained Transformer-based forecasting model. Evaluate the impact on performance across a selection of three real-world datasets (TrafficFlow, USAExchangeRate, SolarEnergy) and study the effects on different adaptation components.
CONTROLS: A baseline without lag or delayed updates, variants with OGD where gradients are estimated from a small batch of recent samples, and models with increased capacity (more layers or attention heads) but no delayed updates.
COST: 3780 
PREDICTION: Expected results will show that more frequent updates can mitigate the negative impact of delayed feedback but at the cost of increased noise in updates; using average or last available gradients might provide a decent compromise between performance and stability.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Adaptive Drift Detection for Triggering Updates in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop an adaptive drift detection method to dynamically decide when to update the model. Design a statistically-driven drift detector based on changes in predictive distributions (e.g., using kernel density estimates or Bayesian methods) to identify significant deviations from the historical patterns. Integrate the detector with the online gradient descent and adapter update strategies from previous proposals to evaluate its impact on performance. Experiment with the adaptive drift detector on three real-world datasets (TrafficFlow, USAExchangeRate, SolarEnergy) using pre-trained Transformer-based forecasting models and evaluate its effectiveness in comparison to a heuristically-driven approach that updates at fixed intervals.
CONTROLS: Baselines from previous proposals (e.g., without update triggers, with fixed update intervals), and variants with the adaptive drift detector but without adapter updates.
COST: 4800 
PREDICTION: Expected results will show that the adaptive drift detector significantly improves performance by reducing unnecessary updates and quickly responding to changes in the data distribution; however, its performance might degrade if the model or data size is too large, making it harder to detect drifts in a timely manner.

ACTION: REVISE 4 
TITLE: Adaptive Drift Detection for Triggering Updates in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Introduce a dynamic threshold to the adaptive drift detection method, allowing the drift detector to adaptively adjust its sensitivity to changes in the predictive distributions. The threshold is learned using a small validation set and updated periodically to ensure the model remains responsive to changes in the data. Experiment with different periodicity and learning rates for the threshold updates and evaluate the impact on performance across three real-world datasets (TrafficFlow, USAExchangeRate, SolarEnergy).
CONTROLS: Baselines from previous proposals, and variants with adaptive drift detection without dynamic threshold.
COST: 5600 
PREDICTION: Expected results will show that the dynamic threshold improves the adaptability and robustness of the adaptive drift detection method; however, it might lead to over-adjustment of the threshold, causing unnecessary updates if the learning rate is too high or the threshold is updated too frequently.

TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Adapters on Model Uncertainty
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of adapters on model uncertainty in online time series forecasting. Use a pre-trained Transformer-based forecasting model and experiment with different adapters (output, input, linear, ensemble weight) on three real-world datasets (TrafficFlow, USAExchangeRate, SolarEnergy). Evaluate the model uncertainty using metrics such as predictive variance, epistemic uncertainty, and aleatoric uncertainty. Compare the results with the baseline model without adapters and analyze the effect of adapters on uncertainty.
CONTROLS: Baselines from previous proposals, and variants with different adapters but without uncertainty metrics.
COST: 6480 
PREDICTION: Expected results will show that adapters tend to reduce model uncertainty, especially for output and input adapters; however, the reduction in uncertainty might come at the cost of increased bias in the model.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Online Gradient Descent with Adapters
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical analysis of online gradient descent (OGD) with adapters for online time series forecasting. Derive a bound on the regret of OGD with adapters, comparing it to the regret of OGD without adapters. Investigate the impact of adapters on the convergence rate of OGD and provide insight into the effect of adapters on the stability of online learning. Assume a fixed but unknown sequence of target functions and prove that the regret of OGD with adapters is upper bounded by a term that accounts for the stability of the adapters and the convergence rate of OGD.
CONTROLS: A baseline without adapters, and variants with different adapters but without theoretical analysis.
COST: 7920 
PREDICTION: Expected results will show that adapters can significantly improve the convergence rate and stability of OGD; however, the theoretical analysis might not fully capture the practical benefits of adapters in online time series forecasting.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Empirical Study of Adapters for Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Conduct an empirical study of adapters for multi-step forecasting, focusing on their ability to adapt to changing patterns and improve forecast accuracy. Experiment with different adapters (output, input, linear, ensemble weight) and evaluation metrics (e.g., MAE, SMAPE, MASE) on a variety of real-world datasets (TrafficFlow, USAExchangeRate, SolarEnergy) and forecasting horizons (1-5 steps ahead). Compare the results with baseline models that do not use adapters and analyze the performance of adapters under different conditions (e.g., high noise, concept drift).
CONTROLS: Baselines from previous proposals, and variants with different adapters but without empirical study.
COST: 9120 
PREDICTION: Expected results will show that adapters can significantly improve forecast accuracy in multi-step forecasting; however, the performance of adapters might degrade in the presence of high noise or concept drift, requiring careful tuning of adapter parameters and hyperparameters.

ACTION: REVISE 7 
TITLE: Empirical Study of Adapters for Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Expand the previous proposal by incorporating the findings from the theoretical analysis (proposal 6) and the adaptive drift detection method (proposal 4). Experiment with different combinations of adapters, theoretical bounds, and adaptive drift detection methods to identify the most effective approach for multi-step forecasting. Evaluate the performance of these approaches on a diverse set of real-world datasets and forecasting horizons, using a comprehensive set of evaluation metrics (e.g., MAE, SMAPE, MASE, MDBI).
CONTROLS: Baselines from previous proposals, variants with different adapters but without combined approach, and a simple adapter-based approach without the theoretical bounds.
COST: 11520 
PREDICTION: Expected results will show that the combined approach significantly improves forecast accuracy and robustness in multi-step forecasting; however, it might come with increased computational cost and require careful tuning of hyperparameters to achieve optimal performance.

TITLE: Exploring Hybrid Retrieval with Text and Image Encoders
PROPOSAL: We will test the effectiveness of combining a state-of-the-art ColPali-based late-interaction multimodal retriever with a lightweight dense text retriever, specifically the AnsiBERT model, on the depuis dataset, which is a common benchmark for visual document retrieval. We will train the ColPali-based model and the Ansibert model individually, then combine their output scores at the representation level, and evaluate the performance of the combined model using metrics such as Recall@1000 and MRR.
CONTROLS: Performance of the ColPali-based model and Ansibert model as individual baselines, as well as a non-combination setting where the two models' output scores are summed.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: We expect the hybrid retrieval model to achieve a higher Recall@1000 score compared to the non-combination setting, while maintaining similar latency and memory requirements, but we anticipate a decrease in performance in cases where the text and image representations are not closely correlated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Designing Architecture-Agnostic Aggregation
PROPOSAL: To enable lightweight and practical combination of retrievers with heterogeneous representations, we propose an architecture-agnostic aggregation method, which consists of a combination-specific embedding layer followed by a dot-product interaction similarity calculation. We test this aggregation method on the same hybrid retrieval setup as in experiment 1, but with varying combinations of ColPali-based and Ansibert models of different dimensionalities and scales.
CONTROLS: Performance of various existing aggregation methods (e.g. element-wise sum, concatenation) and a random aggregation baseline.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: We expect the combination-specific embedding layer to help the aggregation method adapt to the varied representation spaces of the individual retrievers, while achieving a balance between exploitation of the rich query-document interactions and neglect of the complementary signal, and as such, the experiment will demonstrate the validity and robustness of our aggregation method, but may require careful tuning of the layer's parameters to avoid overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Aggregation Methods
PROPOSAL: We theoretically analyze the properties of various aggregation methods, including the combination-specific embedding layer proposed in experiment 2, and derive guarantees on their performance. Specifically, we show that our aggregation method achieves a trade-off between the preservation of the individual models' performance and the exploitation of their complementary signals, and establish an upper bound on its degradation in the presence of noisy or unrelated signals.
CONTROLS: Evaluation of the theoretical bounds against empirical performance on a selection of aggregation methods.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The theoretical analysis will provide insights into the relationships between aggregation methods and the types of performance they preserve/ degrade under different conditions, offering a principled way to evaluate and improve the design of aggregation methods for hybrid retrieval, and demonstrate the expressiveness and power of our proposed aggregation method.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Refining Theoretical Analysis of Aggregation Methods
PROPOSAL: We refine the theoretical analysis of aggregation methods, focusing on their robustness to varying levels of correlation between the signals from different models. By establishing a relationship between the correlation coefficient and the aggregation method's performance, we can provide principled guidelines for selecting aggregation methods that are robust to different types of correlations. Furthermore, we explore the implications of our analysis for designing aggregation methods that are adaptable to dynamic correlations between models.
CONTROLS: Empirical evaluation of the refined analysis against a range of correlation levels and aggregation methods.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: The refined analysis will enable a deeper understanding of how aggregation methods interact with the complex relationships between model signals, providing a stronger foundation for the design of hybrid retrieval systems that can effectively leverage the strengths of multiple models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Robustness to Model Mismatch
PROPOSAL: We evaluate the robustness of our hybrid retrieval system to model mismatch scenarios, where the primary and secondary models are not well-matched or have different strengths and weaknesses. We simulate model mismatch by training the primary ColPali-based model on the full depuis dataset and the secondary Ansibert model on a subset of the data, and assess the impact on the system's performance.
CONTROLS: Performance of the hybrid system under different model mismatch scenarios, including when the primary and secondary models are trained on the same data or when the secondary model is stronger/weaker than the primary model.
COST: 7331.6
PREDICTION: The experiment will reveal how well our hybrid retrieval system can adapt to and compensate for model mismatch, providing valuable insights into the limitations and potential of the approach, and guidance for scenarios where model mismatch might be unavoidable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Domain Adaptation
PROPOSAL: We investigate the role of domain adaptation in hybrid retrieval, where the primary and secondary models are trained on different but related domains. We collect a new dataset, wikimedia26k, which contains images and text from the Wikipedia 26k dataset, and train the primary ColPali-based model on the depuis dataset and the secondary Ansibert model on the wikimedia26k dataset. We then evaluate the performance of the hybrid system on the wikimedia26k test set.
CONTROLS: Performance of the hybrid system under different domain adaptation scenarios, including when the primary and secondary models are trained on the same data or when the secondary model is trained on a novel domain.
COST: 8641
PREDICTION: The experiment will reveal how well our hybrid retrieval system can adapt to and leverage domain knowledge from multiple sources, providing insights into the potential of domain adaptation for improving retrieval performance and the limitations of the current approach.

ACTION: ADD
